title: Risk Register
intro: Two kinds of risk are separated here. Business-as-usual (BAU) risks are the ordinary frictions of owning a single-tenant asset: rollover, credit, rates, taxes. Black-swan risks are low-probability, high-severity events that can reprice or physically damage the asset. Every row carries its evidence and its source; likelihood and impact are assessments, and are labelled as such.

legend.likelihood: Rare (<5%), Unlikely (5-20%), Possible (20-40%), Likely (40-70%), Almost certain (>70%) over the relevant horizon.
legend.impact: Severity on the owner's terminal wealth or on the asset's realisable value.

rows.risk: Tenant is a franchisee, not the corporate brand
rows.evidence: 93.0% of the Jack in the Box system is franchised (1,966 of 2,115 units at 2026-07-05).
rows.likelihood: Almost certain (if PARCEL-01 is a franchised unit, which the owner must confirm)
rows.impact: High — the owner's credit is a single small business, not a national chain with $2.1B+ of revenue.
rows.mitigation: Obtain the lease, the guaranty (if any), and the franchisee's most recent financial statements before any renewal negotiation. Confirm whether the franchisor guarantees the lease.

rows.evidence: Model hazard of 5%/yr before expiry → 18.8% cumulative probability of default by 2030 and 39.9% by 2035 (20,000-path simulation). Franchisor has closed 86 units in FY2025 and guided to 50–100 more in FY2026; franchise bad-debt expense rose.
rows.likelihood: Possible to Likely, depending on expiry year
rows.impact: Medium–High — 12 months of lost rent plus 6% of value in re-letting cost (model assumption).
rows.mitigation: Sell while term remains, or negotiate an early extension with a creditworthy operator. If holding, budget a 12-month vacancy reserve.

rows.risk: Brand-level retrenchment removes this trade area
rows.evidence: FY2026 guidance: 50–100 closures and only ~20 openings; the 2025 'block closure' programme targeted older units. FY2025 same-store sales (4.2%) and Q4 (7.4%).
rows.impact: High — a closed unit converts a bond-like NNN asset into a vacant QSR box in a market with limited drive-thru sites.
rows.mitigation: Ask the franchisor directly whether the unit is on a closure list; the franchisor's own guidance is public, so a buyer will ask the same question.

rows.risk: Owner does not control the renewal decision
rows.evidence: The lease is NNN with expiry 2030–2035 (owner-stated). Renewal options, if any, sit with the tenant — the standard structure in QSR ground/building leases.
rows.impact: High — 'renew the lease' is not a unilateral option; the realistic choices are sell, hold, or offer an inducement to extend.
rows.mitigation: Reframe the decision as sell vs. hold. Any extension requires a negotiated rent, term and TI package.

rows.risk: Cap-rate expansion as long rates rise
rows.evidence: 10-year Treasury 4.84% on 2026-11-05, up from 4.19% on 2026-01-02; 30-year 5.25%; the FOMC raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75–4.00% on 2026-09-17. The modelled going-in cap of 6.00% implies only a 116 bp spread over Treasuries.
rows.impact: High — each +50 bp on a 6.00% cap destroys ~7.7% of value.
rows.mitigation: Sell into the current bid rather than waiting; a shorter lease and a rising-rate backdrop compound the effect.
rows.residual: Transferred to the buyer on sale.

rows.evidence: Modelled: +125 bp on the exit cap and 6% of value in re-letting cost when the tenant vacates.
rows.likelihood: Likely (if the tenant does not renew)
rows.mitigation: Sell with ≥5 years of term; buyers pay for weighted-average lease term.

rows.risk: Property tax reset on sale suppresses the buyer's yield
rows.evidence: Under Proposition 13 a change of ownership generally establishes a new base-year value; the 1% levy applies to assessed value, growth capped at 2%/yr.
rows.impact: Low–Medium — the buyer prices the post-sale tax bill, not the seller's.
rows.mitigation: Model the buyer's reassessed tax in the offering memorandum; do not quote the seller's bill.

rows.risk: Concentration: one asset, one tenant, one block
rows.evidence: A single $X of capital sits in one lease and one building; the model's hold strategies have a 21.8–29.5 (P10) vs 29.4 (P10) spread against the diversified strategy.
rows.mitigation: A §1031 exchange into a diversified net-lease position spreads tenant and geography risk at a higher cash yield.

rows.evidence: Total nonfarm payrolls +0.5% year on year, information sector (5.7%), financial activities (1.7%), government (1.1%); unemployment 4.4%.
rows.impact: Medium — lunch traffic and franchisee margins are the first casualties.
rows.mitigation: Underwrite to the franchised AUV of $1.874M, not to a peak.
rows.residual: Shared with any LA retail asset.

rows.risk: Operating-cost inflation without matching menu pricing
rows.evidence: CPI food away from home +2.8% vs headline CPI 3.7% and energy +20.3%; a 2–3% contractual rent escalator outruns the tenant's pricing power.
rows.impact: Medium — margin compression raises the probability of non-renewal (RK-02).
rows.mitigation: Prefer a flat or CPI-capped structure in any extension, or exit before the next reset.

rows.evidence: LA City base transfer tax 0.45%; Measure ULA adds 4% above $5.4M and 5.5% at/above $10.9M for closings after 2026-06-30.
rows.impact: Low below the ULA threshold; High above it ($436,000 of extra tax on a $10.9M sale).
rows.mitigation: Price the tax into the sale strategy; consider a structure or price point below the threshold where commercially sensible.

rows.evidence: The Los Angeles basin sits in the highest class of the USGS National Seismic Hazard Model; the region has a dense network of active faults. Commercial earthquake cover is usually a separate policy with a significant deductible.
rows.impact: Modelled at 15% of value (deductible, code-upgrade, six months of interruption). A severe event would be far worse and is partly uninsurable.
rows.mitigation: Obtain a seismic (PM L) study and a current CEA/commercial quote; hold in an entity that limits personal liability; carry business-interruption cover.
rows.residual: Cannot be eliminated — only transferred, priced or diversified away from.

rows.risk: Wildfire, smoke event or wind-driven ember intrusion
rows.evidence: In 2025 CAL FIRE recorded 8,232 wildfires, 507,817 acres burned, 31 fatalities and 16,627 structures destroyed statewide; the Palisades (23,448 acres) and Eaton (14,021 acres) fires both burned in Los Angeles County. FEMA declared DR-4856-CA on 2025-01-08.
rows.likelihood: Modelled at 3.0%/yr for a regional disruption
rows.impact: Modelled at 3% of a year's income; a direct burn-over would be catastrophic.
rows.mitigation: Defensible space, Class-A roof, ember-resistant vents; verify the site is outside a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone (requires the address).
rows.residual: Low for an urban central-LA parcel, but not zero — and insurance repricing is already regional.

rows.evidence: The FAIR Plan's residential assessment after the January 2025 fires was $1B and its exposure has grown sharply; press reporting puts policies in force at ~684,000 and exposure in the hundreds of billions. Commercial property is not written by the FAIR Plan, but surplus-lines pricing moves with the same catastrophe load.
rows.impact: Medium — premium and deductible increases reduce NOI at the owner's expense where the lease caps recoveries.
rows.mitigation: Confirm the lease's insurance provisions and whether the tenant or owner carries the policy; obtain a binding quote before closing any sale.

rows.risk: Civil disturbance or prolonged street closure
rows.evidence: Central Los Angeles has experienced repeated protest and closure events; no official statistic quantifies the property-level effect.
rows.impact: Low–Medium (days to weeks of lost trade; physical damage usually insured)
rows.mitigation: Physical hardening; confirm business-interruption coverage; avoid a lease that requires the owner to abate rent for civil authority action.

rows.evidence: Southern California depends on imported water and an ageing grid; drought conditions drive both. No parcel-level official risk score was obtained in this pass.
rows.mitigation: Confirm the tenant carries utility-interruption cover; assess on-site water storage for fire defence.

rows.evidence: The 2020–21 closures demonstrated that a QSR can lose dine-in and late-night trade for a year or more; drive-thru sites retained most of their volume.
rows.mitigation: Drive-thru presence is the single best structural hedge; confirm it exists (PR-10).

rows.risk: Policy shock specific to California QSR
rows.evidence: Sector-specific wage floors and scheduling rules raise the tenant's cost base. The current fast-food wage rate could not be verified from a DIR page in this pass, so no figure is asserted.
rows.impact: Medium — pushes marginal units toward closure, which is exactly the RK-03 mechanism.
rows.mitigation: Track the Fast Food Council's annual determinations; treat any increase as a renewal-probability haircut.
